Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the RFP conversation yesterday. To give you a concrete Dedicated proposal (GPU pool sizing, baseline throughput, and the suggested redundancy/SLA guardrails) we need a short set of workload signals from your side. I attached a one-page questionnaire (lin-corp-sizing-template.xlsx) — if you can return the sheet with values it will let us produce a capacity blueprint and a predictable cost estimate.

Key things that move the needle for sizing:
- Target QPS and 95th/99th percentile request concurrency (requests/sec and concurrent open sessions)
- Typical prompt length and average/95th percentile generated response tokens
- Expected distribution of short vs long requests (e.g., 60% <= 128 tokens, 30% 128–512, 10% >512)
- Peak profile: sustained peak hours/day and any burst windows (duration and recurrence)
- Required latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99 targets) and acceptable tail-degradation policy
- Security/compliance constraints (VPC-only, KMS, audit retention) that affect instance placement

If you prefer, paste a one-week traffic sample (CSV) and we can infer token distribution and concurrency. I dropped a placeholder Google Sheet link in related_links for collaborative editing.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Return the filled sheet or a sample CSV by EOD Tuesday (10/13)
2) We produce a redline capacity blueprint + expected monthly cost and recommended GPU family/quantization options within 48 hours
3) 30-minute call to review and lock mutual action plan

Marissa and Dev are looped for sizing/ops verification.

Thanks —
Sergio Alvarez

Sergio —

Thanks, I received the template. Quick answers to prioritize the fields before we fill the sheet:
- We expect 120 QPS average, with 800 QPS peak bursts that can last up to 20 minutes during business hours (approx. 9am–5pm local).
- Concurrent sessions at p95 are roughly 2,100 (we have long-lived chat sessions aggregated across clients).
- Typical prompt length: 90 tokens median; typical response 180 tokens median. On heavy generation paths (summarization + code), responses can be 1,200–2,000 tokens at the 95th percentile.
- Latency target: p95 <= 350ms for short completions (<256 tokens); for >1k tokens we can accept longer tail but p95 target ~1.5s.
- Security: will need VPC private deployment and KMS for keys; SOC2 plus audit-log retention for 3 years.

Two quick questions for you/your engineers:
1) Which GPU families are you recommending for mixed workloads (short/chat + long-generation)? Is performance materially different between A100/ H100 for our token distribution?
2) Is real-time prefix caching supported across sessions? We have a set of common system prompts and conversation prefixes that we’d like cached.

I’ll ask procurement to fill the attached pricing/procurement sheet once we have your draft blueprint.

—Alice
Director, Applied ML — LinCorp
alice@lincorp.com

Sergio — forwarding Alice's reply with my initial sizing notes.

Summary of what Alice provided (above): 120 QPS baseline, 800 QPS short bursts, p95 concurrency ~2,100; token profile median 90/180, 95th up to 2k tokens. VPC + KMS + 3y audit retention.

Quick sizing sketch / assumptions:
- Model family: recommend H100-like performance profile for mixed long/short workloads. H100 delivers ~1.4–1.8x single-stream throughput vs A100 on long‑token workloads and better latency for batched long generations. If cost constraints are tight we can propose quantized variants on A100xT options as a tradeoff.
- Caching: yes — prefix/KV caching is supported; we can configure per-route cache with shared hot-prefix pools to reduce token compute for common system prompts. That will cut effective cost by up to ~25% in your stated distribution.
- Concurrency mapping: given p95 concurrency ~2,100 and 95th token spikes, initial pool recommendation is 12 x H100 GPUs with a 20% burst buffer (autoscale to +3 GPUs) to keep p95 latency targets. That assumes model X-small/standard (we’ll match exact model once you confirm license). If you choose a heavier model we’ll scale linearly.
- Throughput validation: need a 1-week traffic sample (initial-traffic-sample.csv) so we can run a synthetic replay and calibrate batching + kernel configs. Please share if possible.

Operational notes for proposal:
- SLA and redundancy: 2 AZ placement + automated failover; monthly P95 and P99 SLOs in the proposal; optional hot-standby cluster for critical workloads (adds ~18% to reserve cost).
- Security: Private control plane + KMS integration; audit export hooks — Dev can attach the SOC2 evidence pack and a suggested retention schedule.

Action items I'll take once we get the sheet/sample:
1) Run a 48-hour synthetic replay and produce an expected p95/p99 latency curve and estimated vCPU/GPU token throughput.
2) Produce two pricing options: H100 baseline and A100 quantized discounted variant with expected quality delta.
3) Draft a short Mutual Action Plan (dates for procurement, SOC2 evidence exchange, pilot cutover).

Can you confirm you’ll share the filled template or a one-week sample by EOD Monday 10/18? If so I’ll schedule a 30-minute review for Wed 10/20 at 10am PT and share a draft Mutual Action Plan + a DocuSign link for the preliminary PO/NDAs to speed procurement.

If procurement needs a pricing placeholder to start internal approvals, we can provide an order-of-magnitude monthly reserve figure today — say ~$130k–$180k/month for the H100 baseline with the redundancy profile Marissa described — but final will depend on the exact model and cache hit assumptions.
